title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an identity impersonation fraud in which AI-generated video and imagery were used to replicate the likeness of a real, named attorney and deploy that likeness at scale across social media platforms. The failure mode is not a malfunction of a legitimate AI product but a deliberate misuse of generative tools to produce convincing fake personas. The attack surface was the gap between platform content-moderation systems and the volume of synthetic media that can be created quickly, as nearly 6,500 fake profiles accumulated before a dedicated anti-piracy contractor began removing them.

The harm landed on immigration-seekers who had no reliable mechanism to distinguish the fake profiles from a genuine professional presence, and who faced pressure to pay immediately through peer-to-peer payment apps that offer little recourse. Catching this earlier would have required either automated detection of synthetically generated likenesses at upload time or a faster platform response to reports of impersonation, neither of which appears to have been in place.

What is not established is who is responsible for creating or operating the fraudulent profiles, whether any law enforcement action has been taken, or whether any victims have recovered their money.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles using AI-generated images of Leal to deceive people seeking immigration help. In these fraudulent videos, a digital version of Leal offers services like US residency assistance in exchange for cash payments of around $2,200. The scams typically direct victims to contact numbers through WhatsApp, where fraudsters send fake contracts and collect money through payment apps like Venmo and Zelle.

Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office about services he never offered. Although suspicious activity began last October, the situation has dramatically worsened over the past three months. His firm hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across multiple platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. Leal plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scams. He warns immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and avoid those requesting immediate payment through digital payment apps.
